title: Chapter 132: Uncle Xu Has a Point
html:
Uncle Xu remained worried. “Why can’t we let visitors enter happily and escort them out safely? What’s wrong with that?”

“Okay, okay. Don’t worry, everything is within my control.”

With Uncle Xu’s warnings still ringing in his ears, Chen Ge led the five visitors into the underground garage.

“Please sign these disclaimers first.” Chen Ge passed a few copies to the visitors. “All the notes and warnings are written there. Feel free to browse through them.”

“Very official.” Their leader signed without reading a word. Wang Hailong stood about 1.85 meters tall and appeared close to Chen Ge’s age.

“Boss, you won’t back out of the prize, will you? If someone finds all twenty-four name tags, you’ll actually pay?” The slightly shorter man beside Wang Hailong appeared to be his brother. His name was Wang Wenlong, though the two seemed very different in temperament.

“Of course, where would I be today without honoring my promises?” Chen Ge replied with a professional smile.

“Twenty thousand for one challenger and twenty-four name tags. Since there are five of us, if we find them all, can you give each of us four thousand?” The speaker was Wang Hailong’s girlfriend. She wore a thin blouse and shorts, with a butterfly tattoo at her collarbone. Dou Menglu was pretty, though her handwriting was atrocious.

“Why not? The point is to have fun. Find all the tags within twenty minutes, and each of you will receive the full four thousand.” Chen Ge kept smiling.

Wang Hailong dropped the pen and promised, “Nice! I’ll definitely call my brothers to come support you next time.”

“Then I’ll thank you in advance.”

What a considerate visitor.Chen Ge was touched. “Once you’ve signed, follow me. One word of advice: don’t linger in the sealed classroom.”

At the corridor’s end, Chen Ge removed the boards. “Many rumors surround this abandoned school. Believe them or not, be careful. And remember: no cameras inside. If you ignore that warning, the consequences are yours.”

“It’s underground?” The five peered into the dim passage, where faint sounds suggested someone walking below.

“F*ck, what was that?” The heavyset man who had remained silent cried out and stumbled back. With a beer belly and small eyes, he did not appear especially brave.

“Pei Hu, you’re scared before we’ve even gone in?” Wang Hailong grabbed Pei Hu’s bouncy arm. “It’s all fake. If you’re that scared, hide behind Meili.”

“Stop whining. Are you going in or not?” The other woman spoke with a perpetual frown. She was short, and beside the striking Menglu, even her best efforts left her looking plain. Her waiver identified her as Xia Meili.

“Why the rush?” Wang Hailong winked at Chen Ge. “Boss, don’t start the countdown until we’re inside.”

“Sure.” Chen Ge took out his phone to prepare. After the five visitors entered the tunnel, he closed the boards and put his phone away.

Countdown? What countdown?

Walking out under their own power would be achievement enough. In the dressing room, Chen Ge donned Doctor Skull-cracker’s coat and skin mask, then entered the control room. He reviewed the music list and decided not to loop Black Friday.

Uncle Xu is right. We work in hospitality; the customer comes first.He lowered the volume and added Wedding Dress to the playlist. Repeating one song would only bore them.

…

The boards closed overhead. In the dim corridor, the five visitors stared at half-open classroom doors while shuffling noises drifted around them.

“This place is huge.” Pei Hu edged backward until he stood beside Meili.

“Of course it is. How else could he hide so many tags? The boss isn’t stupid.” Wang Wenlong, the thinnest of them, took the lead. “Let’s move. Five people can find twenty-four tags. Once we win our four thousand each, we’ll celebrate with hot pot and karaoke.”

“We’re already here, so let’s finish it. My brother is right.” Wang Hailong strode ahead, then stopped abruptly beside the first classroom, startling everyone behind him.

“Hailong, what have you seen?” Dou Menglu whispered.

“Look at you. What is there to fear?” He kicked the classroom door open, dislodging a name tag from the frame. “This is easy!”

He picked up the nametag, and a girl’s name was written on it—Chen Yalin.

“He put the first tag somewhere obvious so we’d recognize their shape and size.” Wang Wenlong examined it. “Each should bear a student’s name. The yellowed edges look authentic; reproducing these wouldn’t be easy.”

“What does that matter? We found one in under ten seconds. If we keep calm, the other twenty-three will be easy.” Wang Hailong reclaimed the tag and moved on. Their quick success relaxed the others.

A draft stirred the blank exam papers scattered across the floor. None of the visitors noticed the faint bare footprints appearing on them despite everyone wearing shoes. The temperature fell, and a child’s lullaby crept through the dark corridor, mingling laughter with sobs.

The atmosphere changed. Something seemed to hide in every classroom, countless unseen eyes watching from the dark.

“There’s nothing to be afraid of, but how come I feel weirdly unsettled?”

To search faster, they split up. Xia Meili and Wang Wenlong checked the classrooms on the left while the others searched the right. Several rooms yielded nothing.

“The boss is cleverer than we thought. Keep moving—we can’t waste time.” Wang Hailong took the lead, then froze outside the sealed classroom.

“What’s wrong, Brother Long? Another tag?” Pei Hu followed his gaze and felt cold rush through him. Someone stood at the classroom window, smiling.

Behind that figure, more than twenty mannequins sat or stood throughout the room.

Their bodies remained still, but every neck had twisted at an unnatural angle so they could smile at the visitors beyond the window.
